papers.tier1_role: Context evidence on injection-pressure effects across an HPDI engine map.
papers.study_context: Single-cylinder pilot-ignited direct-injection natural-gas engine experiments over speed, load, and EGR.

cases.description: Injection-pressure comparison across multiple engine conditions.

parameters.definition: Natural-gas injection-pressure levels in the operating-condition matrix.
parameters.notes: Values are shown in Table 5 adjacent to the conclusion.

parameters.reported_value: increased injection pressure enhanced mixing and shortened combustion duration
parameters.definition: Qualitative engine response attributed to mass flux and turbulence.

process_relations.notes: Effect weakens at low load/high differential pressure and with greater engine-speed turbulence.

mechanism_relations.notes: Strongly conditioned by load, speed, and EGR.

evidence_candidates.claim: In this HPDI engine, raising gas injection pressure reduced PM mainly at high load, while low-load emissions and fuel consumption were comparatively insensitive.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Across the tested map, high-load PM mass/number fell and combustion duration shortened; effects diminished with engine speed.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Engine- and operating-map-specific; multiple higher-order interactions were significant.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Historical context for load-dependent pressure benefits.

key_results: At high load PM reductions approached a factor of three; fuel consumption changed little.
mechanisms: Higher pressure increases mass flux and jet-induced turbulence, changing mixing and soot residence/oxidation.
extraction_notes: Tier 3 target question: under what operating conditions does HPDI injection pressure materially affect emissions?

note_fields.Research Question: When does higher gas injection pressure materially change HPDI performance and emissions?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: Single-cylinder heavy-duty engine over speed, load, and EGR.
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: Pressure effects were strongest at high load and weaker at low load or high engine speed.
note_fields.Mechanism Proposed by Authors: Higher pressure increases fuel mass flux and jet-induced turbulence in mixing-controlled combustion.
note_fields.Limitations: Strong operating-condition interactions limit universal transfer.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Context for the dependence of pressure-driven mixing benefits on chamber state and background turbulence.

papers.tier1_role: Context evidence on slightly premixed HPDI emission tradeoffs.
papers.study_context: Single-cylinder HPDI engine experiments with reacting-CFD interpretation.

cases.description: Delayed-pilot slightly premixed combustion versus baseline mixing-controlled HPDI.

parameters.reported_value: slightly premixed combustion by delaying diesel pilot until after NG injection begins
parameters.definition: SPC strategy used to premix more NG before ignition.

parameters.reported_value: baseline >50% versus optimized SPC <10% of fuel in 2<EQR<5 at gas ignition
parameters.definition: Fraction of injected gas in the paper-defined rich zone at ignition.
parameters.notes: CFD trend; ignition timing was not correctly predicted.

process_relations.source_process: delaying pilot relative to NG injection
process_relations.target_process: pre-ignition NG premixing and PM reduction
process_relations.notes: EQR adjustment mitigated methane/NOx tradeoff at the optimized point.

mechanism_relations.notes: Optimized point also had cycle-variation/noise drawbacks.

evidence_candidates.claim: Delaying the diesel pilot to create slightly premixed NG combustion greatly reduced PM, but stable low-PM operation required managing methane, NOx, pressure-rise, and cycle-variation tradeoffs.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: The optimized B75 point removed over 90% PM with about 2% efficiency improvement at similar NOx/methane, but increased cycle variation and peak pressure-rise rate.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Optimized at one mode; CFD did not correctly predict premixed NG ignition.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Context for premixing-based soot control and its stability tradeoffs.

key_results: Optimized SPC removed >90% PM and improved fuel efficiency ~2% at near-baseline NOx and methane.
mechanisms: Premixing reduces the fuel fraction in the rich soot-forming interval at ignition.
extraction_notes: Tier 3 target question: can pre-ignition premixing suppress HPDI soot without unacceptable tradeoffs?

note_fields.Research Question: Can slightly premixed HPDI reduce PM while controlling methane and NOx penalties?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: Single-cylinder engine parameter sweeps supported by reacting CFD.
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: Delayed pilot greatly reduced PM; an optimized point retained NOx/methane but had noise and cycle-variation penalties.
note_fields.Mechanism Proposed by Authors: More premixing leaves less fuel in the rich soot-forming range when gas ignition begins.
note_fields.Limitations: Optimization is mode-specific and CFD did not reproduce premixed NG ignition correctly.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Context for timing-driven premixing as an alternative to purely pressure-driven mixing control.

papers.tier1_role: Context evidence on mixing-versus-chemistry limitation and misfire prediction.
papers.study_context: Detailed-chemistry CFD validated against rapid-compression-expansion-machine measurements.

cases.description: High/low temperature HPDF cases with timing and jet-geometry variation.

parameters.definition: Final compression temperature for high-temperature validation case.

parameters.reported_value: Chalmers-53: 53 species, 244 reactions; reduced from Chalmers-83
parameters.notes: Reported to reduce total compute time about 35%.

process_relations.target_process: transition between mixing-limited and chemistry-limited combustion
process_relations.notes: Complex chemistry mattered more for colder/more premixed states.

mechanism_relations.source_node: gas jet covering low-temperature pilot ignition region
mechanism_relations.target_node: diesel pilot ignition and main-fuel ignition

evidence_candidates.claim: The CFD study found a temperature/premixing boundary between mixing-limited and chemistry-limited HPDF combustion and reproduced low-temperature crossing-jet misfire when the gas jet covered the pilot’s preferred ignition region.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Detailed-chemistry simulations matched RCEM ignition/HRR trends and isolated the H2O2/first-stage-ignition failure mechanism.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Model validation used an RCEM abstraction and reduced injector geometry; A008 machine metadata identity coverage was 0.9091 but PDF identity was visually verified.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Context for regime-dependent model fidelity and interaction-driven misfire.

key_results: Reduced chemistry lowered computation time about 35% for high-temperature cases without material HRR change.
mechanisms: At low temperature the gas jet can cover the pilot core ignition region, preventing sufficient first-stage heat release for main ignition.
extraction_notes: Tier 3 target question: when is HPDF combustion mixing-limited versus chemistry-limited, and how can crossing jets misfire?

note_fields.Research Question: When does detailed chemistry control HPDF combustion, and can the model explain geometry-dependent misfire?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: Detailed-chemistry CFD validated against RCEM timing and geometry cases.
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: High-temperature cases were mostly mixing-limited; colder/more premixed cases became chemistry-sensitive.
note_fields.Mechanism Proposed by Authors: At low temperature a crossing gas jet covers the pilot core ignition region and prevents sufficient first-stage ignition.
note_fields.Limitations: RCEM abstraction and model dependence; machine identity coverage below 1.0 was resolved by visual PDF verification.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Context for separating mixing and chemistry control in pilot/gas interaction.

papers.tier1_role: Context evidence on transient hydrogen-jet penetration and expansion-wave scaling.
papers.study_context: High-frame-rate schlieren measurements of hydrogen injection into a quiescent constant-volume chamber.

cases.description: 52/104 bar hydrogen jets over chamber-density sweep.

process_relations.notes: Penetration rose with pressure and fell with density.

mechanism_relations.notes: Wave structure also observed for nitrogen-in-nitrogen control.

evidence_candidates.claim: Transient underexpanded hydrogen jets showed expansion-wave spacing that scaled with exit-to-chamber pressure ratio, while tip penetration increased with injection pressure and decreased with chamber density.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: High-speed schlieren resolved waves and penetration; a nitrogen-in-nitrogen control separated wave structure from species mixing.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Quiescent chamber and far-field similarity treatment; virtual-origin/near-field corrections remained uncertain.

key_results: All tested jets were underexpanded; nondimensional far-field penetration collapsed approximately with square-root time.
mechanisms: Pressure ratio sets near-field expansion structure; momentum and ambient density set penetration scaling.
extraction_notes: Tier 3 target question: which basic scalings organize transient underexpanded hydrogen jets?

note_fields.Research Question: How do injection pressure and chamber density affect transient underexpanded hydrogen-jet structure and penetration?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: High-speed schlieren in a quiescent constant-volume chamber.
note_fields.Injection / Ambient Conditions: 52 and 104 bar injection; chamber density 1.15–12.8 kg/m3.
note_fields.Wave / Jet Structure: External expansion-wave spacing scaled with exit-to-chamber pressure ratio.
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: Penetration increased with pressure and decreased with density; far-field data collapsed under nondimensionalization.
note_fields.Limitations: Near-field virtual-origin correction and engine transfer remain uncertain.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Context for transient-jet similarity and pressure-ratio-controlled wave structure.

papers.tier1_role: Context evidence on transient methane-jet topology and LES-supported mixing.
papers.study_context: Schlieren experiments and LES of methane injection through a single-hole commercial injector.

cases.description: Methane jets with varied injection pressure and chamber counter-pressure/temperature.

source_locators.notes: Topology, penetration, Mach disk, and mixing results.

parameters.notes: Pressure sweeps paired with chamber-state changes.

parameters.reported_value: subsonic; moderately underexpanded shock cells; highly underexpanded Mach disk and barrel shock
parameters.definition: Three transient flow patterns observed as pressure ratio evolved.

process_relations.source_process: time-varying upstream pressure and NPR during pintle opening
process_relations.notes: Compressibility and pintle motion make Mach-disk height transient.

mechanism_relations.target_node: methane-air mixing in the LES metric
mechanism_relations.notes: Mixing conclusion is numerical and metric-specific.

evidence_candidates.claim: The transient methane jet passed through subsonic, moderately underexpanded, and Mach-disk/barrel-shock topologies as injector/NPR conditions evolved; higher chamber pressure reduced penetration and increased cone angle.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Schlieren and LES agreed on penetration and Mach-disk position, with early-time discrepancies attributed to injector-opening uncertainty.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Single injector and low absolute injection-pressure range; LES opening transient uncertain.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Context for transient topology rather than steady NPR classification.

key_results: Higher injection pressure slightly increased penetration and maximum Mach-disk height; cone angle was nearly unchanged.
mechanisms: Pintle motion and gas compressibility create time-varying upstream pressure and shock structure.
extraction_notes: Tier 3 target question: how does injector opening make an underexpanded methane jet traverse different wave topologies?

note_fields.Research Question: How do injection and chamber conditions shape transient methane-jet penetration, cone angle, Mach disk, and mixing?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: Schlieren in a constant-volume chamber plus LES including internal/external injector flow.
note_fields.Wave / Jet Structure: The transient jet traversed subsonic, shock-cell, and Mach-disk/barrel-shock states.
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: Pressure increased penetration/Mach-disk height; chamber pressure reduced penetration and widened the cone.
note_fields.Limitations: Single injector, modest pressure range, and uncertain opening transient.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Context for time-dependent underexpanded-jet classification and diagnostic/model complementarity.

papers.tier1_role: Context evidence on moderate-Weber breakup regimes and fragment distributions.
papers.study_context: 3D VOF simulations and continuous-air-jet experiments for monodisperse water droplets.

cases.description: Water-drop secondary breakup at We 20–120 and density ratio about 1000.

source_locators.notes: Validated regimes, rim dynamics, and distributions.

parameters.definition: rho_g U_infinity^2 D0 / gamma using initial relative gas/drop velocity, initial diameter, gas density, and surface tension.
parameters.notes: Author range and formula; no project recalculation.

dimensionless_definitions.notes: Author formula and scale meanings are verified; component records are omitted under Tier 3 scope.

process_relations.source_process: rim capillary retraction versus aerodynamic shear
process_relations.target_process: transition from multibag to shear breakup
process_relations.notes: We=80 rim retracts; We=120 rim is sheared downstream.

mechanism_relations.notes: Transition band observed in both simulations and experiments.

evidence_candidates.claim: Across moderate Weber numbers, the bag-to-shear transition was governed by whether capillary retraction stabilized the rim or aerodynamic shear stripped it downstream, with multibag breakup observed in the intervening band.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: 3D VOF and experiments agreed on modes; multibag appeared around 65<We<85 and shear behavior at We=120.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Continuous-air-jet forcing differs from finite-duration shock loading.

key_results: Fragment PDFs were bimodal at lower We and unimodal/lognormal at higher We; reported SMD/MMD about 1.2.
mechanisms: Competition between capillary rim retraction and aerodynamic shear selects transition topology.
extraction_notes: Tier 3 target question: what physical rim dynamics distinguish moderate-We breakup regimes?

note_fields.Research Question: What governs transitions among bag, multibag, and shear breakup at moderate Weber number?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: 3D VOF plus monodisperse water-drop experiments in a continuous air jet.
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: A multibag transition band occurred between bag and shear breakup; fragment PDFs changed with regime.
note_fields.Mechanism Proposed by Authors: Capillary rim retraction competes with downstream aerodynamic shearing.
note_fields.Limitations: Continuous forcing is not equivalent to a finite shock pulse.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Context for interpreting shock-droplet morphologies through established secondary-breakup mechanics.

papers.tier1_role: Context evidence on shock-imprinted droplet internal flow.
papers.study_context: Numerical and theoretical study of a single water droplet under incident shock impact.

cases.description: Shock-strength sweep tracking the internal-flow saddle point.

parameters.reported_value: persistent internal recirculation pattern with a stationary saddle point
parameters.definition: Internal-flow topology established shortly after shock passage.
parameters.notes: Saddle-point position varies with incident shock strength.

process_relations.notes: Authors infer early shock imprint rather than continuous postshock setting.

mechanism_relations.notes: Numerical cases agree with proposed correlation.

evidence_candidates.claim: The simulated droplet internal-flow topology formed soon after shock passage and retained a nearly stationary saddle point whose position correlated with incident shock Mach number.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Numerical trajectories collapsed under the proposed scaling and agreed with the theoretical correlation.
evidence_candidates.limitations: Single water droplet and numerical/theoretical evidence; later breakup was not the main focus.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Context for early shock imprint on later deformation.

key_results: Authors infer that the internal pattern is set during initial shock impact rather than continuously by the postshock stream.
mechanisms: Gas-dynamic impulse establishes a persistent liquid recirculation topology.
extraction_notes: Tier 3 target question: is droplet internal flow set by the initial shock or the sustained postshock stream?

note_fields.Research Question: How does incident-shock strength establish the internal flow of a single droplet?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: Numerical and theoretical water-droplet study tracking an internal saddle point.
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: A persistent internal topology formed quickly; saddle-point location shifted systematically with shock strength.
note_fields.Mechanism Proposed by Authors: The initial shock impulse imprints the internal flow rather than the later postshock stream alone.
note_fields.Limitations: Numerical single-droplet focus and limited treatment of subsequent breakup.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Context for separating impulsive wave effects from sustained aerodynamic loading.

papers.tier1_role: Context evidence on when high-pressure liquid sprays generate shocks in engine-like environments.
papers.study_context: High-speed schlieren of 150 MPa diesel sprays in a high-temperature/high-pressure optical vessel.

cases.description: Ambient temperature/density matrix for injection-generated wave classification.

parameters.definition: Diesel injection pressure used for shock-wave observations.

parameters.reported_value: oblique shock; detached bow shock; acoustic wave; no spray shock
parameters.definition: Observed/predicted wave classes across ambient state and injection ramp-up.
parameters.notes: Acoustic waves are distinguished from shocks.

process_relations.notes: Temperature raises sound speed; density decelerates the tip during injection ramp-up.

mechanism_relations.target_node: whether local spray velocity exceeds sound speed
mechanism_relations.notes: Typical near-TDC engine conditions were judged unfavorable for spray shocks.

evidence_candidates.claim: High ambient temperature and density suppressed diesel-spray shock generation by raising sound speed and decelerating the spray during injection-rate ramp-up; typical near-TDC conditions were therefore unlikely to produce spray shocks.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Schlieren distinguished attached/detached shocks from weak acoustic waves across the ambient matrix.
evidence_candidates.limitations: 150 MPa single-hole injector and vessel conditions; conventional multi-hole injectors have slower ramp-up.
evidence_candidates.potential_chapter_role: Boundary conditions for injector-generated shocks in engines.

key_results: At 600–700 K detached shocks were visible in discussed cases; at 800 K or above only weak acoustic waves were detected.
mechanisms: Shock existence depends on local spray-tip Mach number, itself controlled by sound speed, density-driven deceleration, and injection ramp.
extraction_notes: Tier 3 target question: under which engine-like ambient states can a high-pressure liquid spray remain locally supersonic?

note_fields.Research Question: Do high-pressure diesel sprays generate shocks under engine-like ambient temperature and density?
note_fields.Study Type and Configuration: High-speed schlieren in a high-temperature/high-pressure optical vessel at 150 MPa injection.
note_fields.Wave / Jet Structure: Attached oblique, detached bow, weak acoustic, and no-shock states were distinguished.
note_fields.Main Physical Observations: Temperature raises sound speed; density decelerates the spray and promotes detachment or suppression.
note_fields.Mechanism Proposed by Authors: Shock generation requires local tip velocity to exceed sound speed during rate ramp-up.
note_fields.Limitations: Single-hole research injector and vessel; real multi-hole rate ramps reduce shock likelihood.
note_fields.Relevance to Review Mainline: Contextual boundary for injector-generated shocks versus externally imposed shock–droplet loading.
